text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited tenders for 18,000 tonnes of corn, with the tender closing December 30 and shipment by January 1997.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka's state buying arm the Co-operative Wholesale Establishment has opened a tender for 100,000 tonnes of soft and hard wheat, government officials said. The tender, closing on January 3, is for 50,000 tonnes of soft wheat for delivery in the third week of January and 50,000 tonnes of hard wheat for delivery in the second week of February.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC said it would seek up to 30,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat under its export donation program to Bosnia. The shipment period was slated for January 25-February 20. Offers were due January 7.

- Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. grade-2 or Australian Standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, food ministry officials said on Sunday. The ministry would open offers January 18. Results will be known two to three days later.

WHEAT TENDERS - Yemen postponed until January 7 a soft wheat and soft wheat flour tender initially scheduled for December 26, European grain traders said. Yemen seeks 200,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat flour for shipment between February and June and 200,000 tonnes of new crop U.S. or Canadian or Australian soft white wheat for July-September, they said.

SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The CCC of the USDA said it would tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. Delivery was for February 3-18. Offers were requested by January 7. Successful offerers will be notified January 8.

LENTIL TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade has offered 10,000 tonnes of lentils from the 1996 crops for export, an official spokesman said. He said December 30 was the final date to receive bids and results would be announced December 31.
MARKET TALK - The Philippines is likely to import between 150,000 and 200,000 tonnes of rice in the first quarter of 1997, a senior Department of Agriculture official said.

... Egypt's Port Said authorities said on Thursday they had confiscated an Algerian cargo ship on suspicion that its cargo of French wheat also contained poppy pods, from which opium is extracted. They said the ship was carrying 52,500 tonnes of French wheat.
